result.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds FTRL for Linear Bandits: The Interplay of Information Acquisition, Corruption, and Geometry
result.summary: We study \textit{best-of-both-worlds} (BOBW) algorithms for linear bandits, which aim to simultaneously guarantee $\gO(\sqrt T)$ regret in the adversarial regime and $\gO(\log T)$ regret in the stochastic regime over $T$ rounds. For finite action sets, we introduce \emph{information-acquisition follow-the-regularized-leader} (\IAFTRL{}), the first BOBW algorithm based purely on the follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) framework that attains an $\gO(\cstar\log T)$-type regret in the stochastic regime, where $\cstar$ is the information-acquisition complexity that characterizes instance-dependent optimality in linear bandits, while retaining the $\gO(\sqrt{T})$ regret guarantee in the adversarial regime. This resolves the open problem posed in~\cite{LeeEtAl2021,KongZ023,ItoT23,ZhaoItoLi2025}.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究线性 bandit 的 best-of-both-worlds 保证，提出纯 FTRL 框架的 IAFTRL 算法，在有限动作集上同时取得对抗情形的 O(√T) 与随机情形 O(C*log T) 型遗憾，其中 C* 为刻画实例最优性的信息获取复杂度。
AI.relevance_reason: 「信息获取复杂度」可视为对信息价值的实例化度量，或可供核查其与 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡、证据获取何时值得的评价思路之间的概念联系；但文中的几何指动作集结构而非 latent 表示几何，迁移程度需自行判断。
